description: VÆLORA is an immersive 3D space exploration web application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It combines real-time spectroscopic sky data with interactive spherical planet simulations, allowing users to pilot round exoplanets with atmospheric glow, customize their astronaut avatars and suits, and inspect near-infrared survey telemetry across hundreds of millions of galaxies.
summary: What if anyone could hunt for "Planet X" or analyze deep-space infrared spectra right from their browser? As a solo creator, I built VÆLORA, an immersive, all-in-one web platform that transforms NASA’s complex 102-band SPHEREx spectrophotometric survey data into an intuitive, gamified universe where users can track fast-moving brown dwarfs and explore the outer boundaries of our solar system. VÆLORA addresses the challenge by democratizing heavy astrophysical data into a visual, interactive sky map where users can dynamically toggle wavelength bands and blink survey epochs to uncover hidden trans-Neptunian objects. To make the experience deeply engaging, explorers can customize realistic astronaut avatars linked to 16 MBTI mission archetypes, test their knowledge with space trivia, and pilot probes through the Kuiper Belt Arcade. VÆLORA wins because it proves what a single developer can achieve by combining rigorous scientific accuracy with game mechanics, creating an unforgettable experience that makes space science irresistible, accessible, and thrilling for the next generation of discoverers.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

VÆLORA is an interactive, browser-based deep-universe and exoplanet exploration platform powered by simulated and benchmark spectrophotometric concepts from NASA’s SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer) mission.

The platform brings four core modules together into a single, seamless web application:

1. SPHEREx Sky Viewer: Users can inspect real astronomical benchmarks (such as the ultra-cold Y-dwarf WISE 0855 and Barnard's Star) across 102 near-infrared spectral channels spanning 0.75 mu to 5.0 mu. By adjusting the wavelength slider, explorers can observe deep molecular absorption bands (like methane at 3.20 mu), and by clicking "Blink Epochs," users can visually compare observations over time to spot high-proper-motion objects and potential Planet X candidates.

2. Realistic Astronaut & Suit Customizer: Users build their own dynamic SVG astronaut avatar—customizing facial features, hair, skin tones, and EVA suit themes—while pairing their profile with an orbital mission specialty.

3. Cosmic 16-Personalities (MBTI) Diagnostic: An interactive, space-scenario personality assessment that maps users to one of 16 specialized NASA mission archetypes (such as Master Astrometric Architect) and rewards them with in-app Cosmic Credits.

4. Cosmic Arcade: A gamified learning hub featuring a space science trivia bank and a real-time HTML5 Canvas Kuiper Belt Probe mini-game where players navigate hazardous outer-solar-system debris fields.

What Benefits Does It Have?

Bullet Democratizes Complex Telemetry: Professional astronomical FITS files and multi-band infrared spectra usually require specialized software and coding knowledge to interpret. VÆLORA translates those data points into instant, visual sliders and interactive animations anyone can understand.

Bullet Zero-Barrier Access: Because it runs directly in any modern desktop or mobile web browser with zero downloads or installations required, students, teachers, and space enthusiasts can start exploring immediately.

Bullet Active Learning Over Passive Reading: Instead of reading static articles about infrared astronomy or proper motion, users actively manipulate wavelengths, blink sky epochs, and test their knowledge through trivia and arcade challenges.

What Is the Intended Impact?

VÆLORA is designed to bridge the gap between cutting-edge NASA astrophysics and public curiosity. With SPHEREx actively conducting its all-sky near-infrared survey, the mission is generating massive amounts of data. VÆLORA’s goal is to inspire the next generation of citizen scientists, students, and young explorers by turning real outer-solar-system science into an engaging, personal adventure. By showing users how astronomers actually hunt for hidden brown dwarfs and trans-Neptunian objects, it empowers anyone to see themselves as a future space explorer. 

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

Bullet Core Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) for lightweight, ultra-fast browser execution without heavy framework overhead.

Bullet Graphics & Visualization: HTML5 <canvas> API (used for the real-time Kuiper Belt Arcade physics/collision loop and interactive starfield backgrounds) and dynamic, layered inline SVG rendering (used for the customizable astronaut avatars and spectral data plots).

Bullet Scientific Data & Reference: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) SPHEREx mission parameters (0.75–5.0 mu spectral bands, resolution profiles, and proper motion benchmarks). 

Bullet Development & Production Tools: Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub for version control, and browser developer tools for responsive mobile/desktop layout optimization and frame-rate debugging.

How Is This Project Creative?

Most space apps fall into one of two categories: dry scientific data tables or purely fictional space games. VÆLORA creatively fuses both worlds.

Bullet Instead of treating science and gamification separately, VÆLORA connects them through a unified progression system (Cosmic Credits earned in the personality diagnostic and arcade) and a narrative identity (your custom astronaut avatar and MBTI mission role).

Bullet Using interactive "Epoch Blinking"—a classic astronomical discovery technique used to find Pluto—and pairing it with a live near-infrared wavelength scrubber turns an advanced astrophysics concept into a tactile, detective-like experience.

What Factors Were Considered During Development?

As a solo creator, every architectural and design decision had to balance scientific depth with usability and performance:

Bullet User Experience (UX) & Accessibility: I designed a clean, high-contrast "deep space" dark interface with responsive navigation so the app works smoothly on both desktop monitors and mobile touchscreens (including dedicated touch controls for the arcade game).

Bullet Performance & Reliability: Building the graphics natively with SVG and HTML5 Canvas ensured instant loading times and smooth 60fps animations without relying on external servers that could lag during live demonstrations.

Bullet Scientific Authenticity vs. Simplicity: I carefully selected real astronomical targets (like WISE 0855) and accurate SPHEREx wavelength ranges so the educational value remains authentic while keeping the controls intuitive enough for a first-time user to master in seconds.
